HMLR_S4_UPDATED_20260601
Practice Guide 40 supplement 4 was updated on 1 June 2026.
HMLR_S4_ENGLAND_WALES
The supplement applies to England and Wales.
HMLR_GENERAL_BOUNDARIES_MAJORITY
Registration with general boundaries is sufficient for the majority of titles.
HMLR_TWO_PRECISION_ROUTES
The two main routes to greater precision are a boundary agreement and a determined boundary.
HMLR_AGREEMENT_PROCESS_DISPUTE_RISK
The process of agreeing an exact boundary can itself generate disagreement or a boundary dispute.
HMLR_OWNERS_CAN_AGREE
Two or more sets of owners may agree the boundary between their properties.
HMLR_AGREEMENT_POSITION
A boundary agreement may address the position of the legal boundary.
HMLR_AGREEMENT_MAINTENANCE
A boundary agreement may also address maintenance of a boundary feature.
HMLR_LEGAL_ADVICE_ROLE
Legal advisers determine whether an agreement is appropriate, its form and whether to apply for register entry.
HMLR_PLAN_QUALITY_HELPFUL
A higher-quality plan showing the legal boundary more precisely is likely to be more useful to successors.
HMLR_PLAN_SIGNATURE_DATE
It is sensible for the parties and witnesses to sign and date the plan attached to an agreement.
HMLR_PLAN_SUPPLEMENT2_GUIDANCE
An agreement plan may be prepared using the plan guidelines in Practice Guide 40 supplement 2.
HMLR_WORDS_ONLY_POSSIBLE
A plan is not always essential because a boundary may sometimes be identified sufficiently in words.
HMLR_MORTGAGEE_GENERALLY_NOT_PARTY
A mortgagee will generally not need to be a party to a boundary agreement.
HMLR_DETERMINED_S60_EXACT_LINE
A determined boundary records the exact line of a registered estate boundary under section 60.
HMLR_ACT_EXACT_UNDEFINED
The Land Registration Act 2002 does not define the word exact for a determined boundary.
HMLR_NOT_DISPUTE_DECIDER
HM Land Registry does not determine where a disputed exact boundary lies.
HMLR_LINE_IDENTIFIED_FIRST
The exact boundary line must be identified before HM Land Registry records it as determined.
HMLR_REGISTER_EACH_TITLE
The property register of each affected title refers to the determined boundary.
HMLR_TITLE_PLAN_GENERAL_POSITION
The title plan marks the general position of the determined boundary, often using lettered points.
HMLR_FILED_PLAN_RETAINED
A filed copy of the determined-boundary plan is retained to identify the exact line.
HMLR_EXPERT_REPORT_ROUTE
An expert report identifying the legal boundary can support a determined-boundary application.
HMLR_AVAILABLE_EVIDENCE
The exact line is identified from the evidence available.
HMLR_PLAN_OR_DESCRIPTION
The line must be identified by a plan, or by a plan together with a verbal description.
HMLR_SURROUNDING_FEATURES
The plan must show enough surrounding physical features to locate the boundary generally on the Ordnance Survey map.
HMLR_IDENTIFY_ADJOINING_OWNERS
All owners of land adjoining the boundary must be identified.
HMLR_OWNER_DEFINITION
For notice purposes owners include freeholders, leaseholders and holders of a registered charge.
HMLR_UNREGISTERED_DOC_TITLE
For unregistered adjoining land the applicant must provide evidence of the adjoining owner's documentary title.
HMLR_DEEDS_CONFLICT_CHECK
Adjoining deeds are checked for evidence showing the boundary in a different position.
HMLR_INTERVENING_THIRD_PARTY_STRIP
A third party may own a strip between properties even when title-plan red edging appears adjoining.
HMLR_ONE_TRANSACTION
Only one Determined Boundary transaction is needed regardless of the number of adjoining boundaries.
HMLR_FIXED_FEE
A fixed fee is payable for a determined-boundary application.
HMLR_REGISTRAR_PLAN_TEST
The registrar must be satisfied that the plan identifies the exact line claimed.
HMLR_REGISTRAR_ARGUABLE_CASE
The registrar must be satisfied that the applicant has an arguable case for the line shown.
HMLR_REGISTRAR_OWNER_NOTICE_TEST
The registrar must be able to identify adjoining owners and an address for notice.
HMLR_NOTICE_EXCEPTIONS
Notice is not required where the lodged evidence includes a written adjoining-owner agreement or a court order.
HMLR_OBJECTION_TRIBUNAL
A non-groundless objection is referred to the First-tier Tribunal unless the parties reach agreement.
HMLR_PROFESSIONAL_PLAN_RECOMMENDED
A chartered land surveyor or other suitably qualified professional should normally prepare the determined-boundary plan.
